newsitem.title: USA: Harvard gets gift of $22 million.
newsitem.headline: Harvard gets gift of $22 million.

text.p: Leveraged buyout specialist Thomas Lee of Boston has donated $22 million to Harvard University, the university said on Monday.
In an extraordinary degree of flexibility, the 1965 graduate is allowing the school to decide how $19 million of the gift should be spent, he said.

"It's really got as few strings as possible. I let them do what they want to do with the $19 million," Lee, who received a bachelor of arts in economics, told Reuters. He said he made the gift in April but the university waited to announce it.

He designated $1 million to go to the Harvard Graduate School of Education, $500,000 each to the American Repertory Theatre and the Fogg Art Museum and $500,000 each to two medical institutions affiliated with Harvard -- Beth Israel Hospital and the Dana Farber Cancer Institute.
"Giving something back is not something that just came to me. If, by luck, you're successful you do have to give something back," he said.
Lee's Boston-based firm, Thomas H. Lee Company, participated in leveraged buyouts of General Nutrition Inc., Playtex Family Products, First Alert and Snapple Beverages.

In leveraged buyouts, firms pay for takeovers by putting up a small amount of capital and borrowing the rest of the money to complete the deal. They profit when the companies go public again or are sold.
